text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a recurring delta (~0.6%-1.4%) between token counts in route-proxy logs and the billing dashboard for EU prod tenants this morning. Root metrics diverge after the route fallback window. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: Hmm, which pipeline? streaming or finalizer?

maya: streaming (route-proxy -> event-collector -> aggregator). The discrepancy shows up in invoice-preview for customers using fallback routing (model-alias -> fallback-small).

leo: Can you paste an example tenant id + sample event IDs?

maya: tenant=org_9EU, sample events: 01FJ2...a9, 01FJ2...b2. From proxy log: tokens=1,254,302. Dashboard preview: 1,240,109.

alina: That looks like token attribution lost during fanout to sidecar dedupe? We had a recent canary that changed fingerprint key ordering.

maya: exact. Canary hash-order tweak landed 2d ago. @sam did a canary revert yesterday but maybe partial.

sam: I rolled back the canary on gateway-level but aggregator still had the change for some partitions. Checking.

billing-bot: Note: invoice-preview job run at 2026-03-19T05:20Z. Backfill available via /admin/backfill.

thomas: If this is ordering-dependent, dedupe key should be idempotent. Proposed quick fix: include monotonically increasing seq from proxy in fingerprint.

irene: Risk: seq increases event size and could change batching behavior. Could we instead canonicalize fields used in fingerprint (sorted headers + model alias)?

leo: Also check the sampler. We recently changed 0.1% sampling to prioritize long sessions; if aggregator extrapolation expects uniform sampling it will bias estimates.

maya: Good catch — org_9EU has many long sessions. sampler config: `sampler.policy: tail_prefer,rate:0.1`

sam: Ok reproducing locally with recorded traffic. Steps: 1) replay proxy subset into staging collector 2) run aggregator with old/new fingerprint 3) compare ledger deltas.

maya: I ran a lightweight replay — deltas align when using old fingerprint, diverge with new one. So it's fingerprint permutation causing double-deduping/miss.

thomas: Action: hotfix aggregator to treat fingerprint as unordered set (use sorted concatenation) — minimal CPU cost. Then schedule proper rollout with unit tests.

alina: Also: console UX for invoice-preview should show "estimation model" and sampling config used. Right now it's opaque and triggers support tickets.

irene: I can add a small badge and hover tooltip: "preview uses sampler X; see /docs/billing/sampling". Low risk.

sam: I'll patch aggregator in canary partition, run replay twice, and open a roll-forward PR. ETA 2h.

maya: Thanks. If hotfix reduces delta we should run quick backfill for affected tenants for last 48h.

ops-sre: FYI we're watching CPU on aggregator nodes — hotfix may change cache keys briefly. I'll stand by auto-scale.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/aggregator/pull/438 — adds ordered-canonicalization for fingerprint and a feature flag `billing.fingerprint_ordered=false` (default false).

maya: After deploy to canary, I'll re-run invoice-preview compare and post numbers here.

leo: One more: add a quick metric `billing.fingerprint_mismatch_rate` when dedupe result differs between old/new key perms so we can alert automatically.

maya: agreed. logging: `fingerprint.compare_result=changed` with tenant tag.

thomas: Postmortem note: document the invariant that fingerprint must be independent of header ordering; add unit test with randomized header orders.

maya: Perfect. I'll message support to hold off on contacting customers until we confirm backfill. :+1:

sam: Deployed canary patch to 3 partitions, collecting logs. Will update in ~30m.

billing-bot: Backfill queue item created: backfill/tenant/org_9EU/48h/job_20260319_1930

maya: Initial canary shows 0.2% delta vs 1.1% before. Looks promising. I'll coordinate backfill once patch goes to prod.

irene: I'll raise a console PR for the sampler badge. Small copy: 'Estimate based on recent sampled traffic — may differ from final invoice.'

maya: Thanks all. Closing once backfill done and dashboard update merged.
